title: Platform Tutorial Review
description: Test your understanding of how to use the learning platform.

questions.question: Where do you write your Python code on this platform?
options: In a separate application you need to install
In the code editor in your web browser
On paper, then type it into a special converter
In the terminal only
questions.explanation: You write Python code directly in the browser-based code editor. No installation needed - everything runs in your web browser!

questions.question: What's the difference between 'Run Code' and 'Submit Code'?
options: 'Run Code' is for testing, 'Submit Code' checks correctness and awards XP
'Run Code' is slower but more accurate
'Submit Code' only works for theory lessons
There's no difference - they're the same button with different labels
questions.explanation: 'Run Code' lets you test your code freely. 'Submit Code' validates it against test cases and awards XP if correct. Use 'Run Code' to experiment, then 'Submit Code' to complete the lesson.

questions.question: How do you navigate to the next lesson?
options: Close the browser and reopen it
Use the 'Next Lesson' button that appears after completing the current lesson
Always use the browser's back button
Lessons automatically advance after 5 minutes
questions.explanation: After completing a lesson (including any required quiz/exercise), a 'Next Lesson' button appears. Click it to continue your learning journey in the correct sequence.

questions.question: What keyboard shortcut runs your Python code?
options: Ctrl+S (Save)
F5 (Refresh)
Ctrl+Enter (Run)
Alt+F4 (Close)
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on Mac) is the keyboard shortcut to run your code. This lets you test quickly without taking your hands off the keyboard.

questions.question: Where do you see the output of your Python program?
options: In a pop-up window
In the terminal below the editor
In your browser's console (F12)
It's emailed to you
questions.explanation: Program output appears in the terminal panel below the code editor. This includes print() statements, calculation results, and any error messages.

questions.question: How can you quickly clear the terminal output?
options: Restart your computer
Press Ctrl+L or click the Clear button
Type 'delete everything' and press Enter
Terminal clears automatically every hour
questions.explanation: Ctrl+L (Cmd+L on Mac) or the Clear button instantly clears all terminal output, giving you a fresh workspace.

questions.question: What do XP points represent?
options: Extra Problems (additional exercises)
Experience Points (earned for progress)
Example Programs (sample code)
Exit Points (ways to leave the platform)
questions.explanation: XP stands for Experience Points. You earn them by completing lessons, exercises, and quizzes. They gamify your learning and track your progress.

questions.question: When does a module's final quiz become available?
options: Immediately when you start the module
After completing the first lesson
After completing all lessons in the module
Only on weekends
questions.explanation: The module quiz unlocks only after you've completed all lessons within that module. This ensures you've learned all concepts before being tested.

questions.question: What's the purpose of the 'Review Mode' toggle?
options: To delete your progress and start over
To revisit completed lessons without affecting progress
To make the text larger for better readability
To switch between light and dark themes
questions.explanation: Review Mode lets you revisit any completed lesson to reinforce learning. You can re-read content and redo exercises without affecting your original progress or XP.

questions.question: How is the course structured?
options: 20 random topics in no particular order
3 phases: Fundamentals, Intermediate, and Projects
Only advanced topics for experienced programmers
Just a collection of unrelated coding challenges
questions.explanation: The course has 20 modules organized into 3 logical phases: Phase 1 (Fundamentals: Modules 1-10), Phase 2 (Intermediate: Modules 11-15), and Phase 3 (Projects: Modules 16-20).
